name: Z-Squish
summary: Go-Go with the stretching moved from the arm to the world: the hand stays where it really is, and the scene is compressed along the viewing direction so the hand reaches the same far points Go-Go would.
howItWorks: The mechanics are Go-Go's: beyond a fixed radius, the reach is multiplied non-linearly. Instead of showing a stretched virtual arm, Z-Squish renders the hand at its real position and compresses the scene along the camera-to-hand axis by the inverse of the Go-Go mapping, so whatever the Go-Go hand would touch now lies under the real hand. A sphere cursor matching the rendered hand selects with the controller trigger. In a study with 18 participants on a Quest 3, selection time and misclicks were comparable to Go-Go, and unlike Go-Go, time was not affected by target size or distance.
advantages: The rendered hand stays at its real position.
Performance matched Go-Go in the study.
limitations: The world visibly deforms as the hand moves.

relationships.note: Go-Go's distance multiplier is kept unchanged; only what the user sees changes.
Introduced and compared in the same study.
